Confirmed.

The lines are at the named places and run as bright-dark pairs along every softbox edge, the curved band and the short vertical line at x ~971. They are jagged where the OFF edges are smooth.

They cannot be the reflections. Added reflected light can only lighten the glow, yet the dark side drops 5-11 R levels below both neighbours where the softbox adds only 0-3 R levels. The real reflections are the faint filled faces, with G and B raised.

Visibility by size:
- At 100 % they read as stitched seams or cracks.

- In the 300 px row they merge into the glow's mottle; the cleaned copy keeps that texture too.

(a) The OFF frame is not free of the profile. The same thin lines sit in its red channel at the same places, at about the same 8-bit strength. Strong real edges hide them at the softbox outlines. Along the curved band the OFF draws a faint thin line at the sharp start of the horizon change; it is not only a soft 30 px change.
(b) "The lines will be about 1.4x stronger" in LIT-b is not supported. The filled faces will be about 1.39x stronger relative to the glow: the studio is raised 1.39x, then everything drops 0.48 EV, so the studio ends where it is and the glow falls to 0.72. But the lines have the same strength in the OFF frame, where the studio light is about 5-6 EV brighter. So they do not follow the studio light; expect about today's strength relative to the glow. Either way, the re-balance will not remove them.

What they most likely are: denoiser artifacts at the reflection's edges. The likeliest source is the albedo/normal guide passes, which hold those edges at full contrast whatever the exposure. They are not softboxes focused through the shell onto the opal: that light would pass the red tint and carry no green or blue, would be blurred, and would not line up at 0 px with the outer-surface reflection. They repeat almost exactly from round 4, so they are not random from render to render. This is the best reading, not proof.

Hiding the softboxes from glossy rays would remove the softbox outlines. The curved band and the vertical line, which follow other reflected edges, would probably stay. A denoiser-off or guide-free crop is the test.

found.outlines_cause:
Most likely denoiser artifacts along the edges of the studio as reflected in each lamp.

Their layout is real. They sit within 0-3 px of each lamp's own softbox reflections in its OFF frame, on the sphere and on the dome alike, each following its own surface. So they follow the polished outer surface's mirror geometry. That rules out two causes:
- A caustic of the softboxes on the opal would land elsewhere, and broad and soft through a concentric 6 mm shell.
- A refraction is impossible, because the softboxes stand in front of the lamps.

Their form is not a reflection's, or a housing's, flag's or cutter's:
- They dip up to about 2 L* below the outside, and a reflection only adds light.
- They are dashed light-dark zippers wandering 0-3 px, where the OFF frames have clean anti-aliased steps and no dark frame line.
- They also appear where the reflected light has no edge: the Core's curved band along the soft horizon, and the pendant's two vertical lines down to the rim. These are missing from the OFF frames' G channel, which carries only the white reflection, and present in the R channel of both OFF and LIT.

A denoiser told about edges by its albedo/normal guide passes does exactly this. The guides carry the reflected studio at full strength at any exposure, while the lit frame's light barely changes across those edges. The round-4 frames carry the same seams at the same strength, so this round's fixes did not cause them. The glow's 10-25 px blotches are the same denoiser's residue.

The lighter rectangle and the faint lift inside the trapezoids are the real reflections: G and B rise exactly at the studio's -4.3 to -5.2 EV scale. But R also rises 4-5 times more inside the shapes than a reflection would give, likely the same artifact.

A real photograph of these lamps in this studio would show only faint, clean-edged lighter patches in those places, with no outlines.

I could not refute it.
- The place is right and every profile reproduces within about 1 L*.
- It is not one of the three known items.
- The physics is wrong: in this frame the studio contributes only about 5 % of its OFF light, so no reflection of a housing, flag, cutter or softbox can draw a 2.5-4.5 L* groove where OFF has a step. - The lines line up with the OFF reflection edges to 1-3 px. They are jagged and change sign along each edge. They sit in the same layout in both lit frames, and they moved with the reflections between rounds.
- Most likely they are denoiser artifacts. The polished shell shows the studio's edges sharply in the denoiser's albedo and normal guide passes, while the noisy glow underneath has almost no edge there. The adaptive-threshold sampling may add to it. A quick test is a LIT render with denoising off, or denoised from color only: if the lines vanish, that is the cause.
- It is blocking: at 480x600 on a plain 1x screen the opal shows crackle veins, at 2x and at 100 % it reads as crackle glass with window shapes drawn on it, and that misstates a smooth opal ball.

Two parts are overstated:
- The mottle is real but only 1.2-1.5 times the pendant's in my band, and no worse than round 4. The lines are what makes this blocking.
- The -0.48 EV re-balance: 2^0.48 = 1.395 is right. The lines kept the same depth across round 4 to round 5 (about 1 EV), so the re-balance will not remove them at 100 %. Its 1.39 times stronger fills may hide them a little at 480, as the stronger fills did in round 4. So core-ember-lit-b needs the 100 % and 480 look the critic asks for.
